cells.verb: letting the mind settle instead of churn
cells.place: at an ending that has to finish before the next thing can start
cells.ask: Pass on what this ending taught you to one person who's standing near their own — in words shaped for them, not the words you'd have used a year ago. What comes back is a quiet that doesn't just belong to you anymore.
cells.core:
Something is closing, and your mind has gone quiet about it. Not numb, and not pretending it isn't over — just settled, the way a room gets when the last box is out and you can finally hear the house. You're letting it finish without narrating it to death, and that's doing the healing on its own.

That kind of quiet is rare enough to be worth more than keeping. Someone near you is at a door of their own, and what you've learned here would help — if it arrives in a shape that fits them rather than you.
cells.sheetLine: Your mind can rest while the thing ends. That rest is worth handing on.

cells.tense: Future — bracing against a next part that hasn't been written yet.
cells.verb: forcing the mind quiet before it's ready
cells.place: at an ending you've declared finished before it actually is
cells.ask: Let one honest feeling about this ending pick a direction, and take one real step that way — toward it or away from it, but moving. What comes back is a calm you didn't have to hold in place: steady enough to carry the mess instead of flattening it.
cells.core:
You've announced to yourself that you're at peace with this ending. The trouble is the ending hasn't quite happened, and the peace is doing a job — it's a lid, held down against whatever comes next. The stillness isn't rest. It's a brace.

A mind that's actually settled doesn't have to keep checking that it's settled. Yours is checking. The calm you want is on the other side of letting something in you move first.
cells.sheetLine: You're calling it peace. It's a lid.

cells.tense: Past — still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: unable to let the mind come to rest
cells.place: at an ending that's already over, with the handle still in your hand
cells.ask: Don't try to make your mind be quiet; it won't take the order. Instead, let yourself feel the pull of one person or one thing on this side of the door — just the curiosity, just what you might want to feel toward them, without having to land anywhere. What comes back, sideways, is the mind going still on its own, steady enough to hold what's finished and what's next at once.
cells.core:
The thing is over. You know that. And your mind won't put it down — it keeps turning it, replaying it, looking for the version where it closes cleaner. You're standing at a door that already shut behind you, and the turning has become a way of not stepping into the room you're actually in.

You can't think your way to quiet; that's more of the same turning. The rest arrives from a different direction entirely.
cells.sheetLine: It's already over. Your mind hasn't been told.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down in a room you're already writing in.
cells.verb: the mind already settled, without being credited for it
cells.place: at an ending you've privately finished but keep describing as open
cells.ask: Tell one person it's over — plain, in your own words, without the explanation you've rehearsed. What comes back is the quiet you already have, now out in the open where it can hold the rest of your life steady too.
cells.core:
You've already come to rest about this. The ending happened, something in you accepted it, and your mind has stopped working the problem — you can feel it in how little it costs you now. But when it comes up, you still talk like you're torn, like it's a question you're sitting with.

The settling got done. The saying-so didn't. And the gap between them is where the rest of your attention keeps leaking.
cells.sheetLine: You've already let it go. You're still saying you haven't.
